contentBlocks.body: TypeScript classes are JavaScript classes with types on their fields, parameters, and return values, plus access modifiers that control who may touch a member. public (the default) is visible everywhere, protected is visible in the class and its subclasses, and private only inside the class that declares it. readonly means the field can be assigned in its declaration or the constructor and never again.

Parameter properties are a shorthand: putting a modifier on a constructor parameter declares the field and assigns it in one step. constructor(readonly name: string, private clock: () => number) {} is the same as declaring both fields and assigning them in the body.

The important catch: private, protected, and readonly are checked only by the compiler. They are erased from the JavaScript output, so at runtime (session as any).now still works, and JSON.stringify still includes private fields. JavaScript's own #private fields are enforced by the engine at runtime. Use TypeScript modifiers for design intent inside a codebase, and #fields when privacy must hold at runtime too.
An abstract class cannot be instantiated and can declare abstract methods that subclasses must implement. Use one when subclasses share real code; if they only share a shape, an interface is lighter.
readonly is shallow. readonly items: string[] stops you reassigning items, but items.push("x") still compiles. Use readonly string[] (or ReadonlyArray<string>) to block mutation of the array itself.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Where can a protected member be accessed?

choices: inside the declaring class and its subclasses
payload.answer: inside the declaring class and its subclasses
payload.explanation: protected sits between private (declaring class only) and public (everywhere).

knowledgeItems.prompt: What happens to a TypeScript private field in the emitted JavaScript?

choices: it is removed from the object
the modifier is erased; the field is an ordinary property at runtime
payload.answer: the modifier is erased; the field is an ordinary property at runtime
payload.explanation: Access modifiers are compile-time only. Use #fields for runtime privacy.

knowledgeItems.prompt: What does constructor(readonly id: string) {} declare?

choices: a readonly public field id, assigned from the argument
payload.answer: a readonly public field id, assigned from the argument
payload.explanation: A modifier on a constructor parameter turns it into a parameter property.

knowledgeItems.prompt: With readonly tags: string[], which line still compiles?

payload.explanation: readonly protects the property binding, not the array it points to.

payload.text: A field marked ____ can be read by subclasses but not by code outside the class hierarchy.
